target.title: fix(gateway): re-check session runtime model against current agent defaults after hot-reload
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent model hot-reload (`agents.<id>.model.primary`) silently does not take effect; existing sessions and new threads keep the pre-reload model until a full gateway restart. Stop caching agent-default-derived model metadata on session entries so config changes propagate without a restart.

- Problem: During every session reset (`performGatewaySessionReset`), the resolved model was unconditionally written as `modelProvider`/`model` on the session entry. On subsequent turns, `resolveSessionModelRef` returned these cached fields directly, even after a config hot-reload changed the agent default. New child sessions inherited the stale values through `inheritSessionRuntimeSelection`.
- Solution: During session reset, only write `modelProvider`/`model` when the resolved model came from a user-preserved override (`providerOverride`/`modelOverride`). When the resolved model reflects the agent default, leave the fields undefined so `resolveSessionModelRef` falls through to `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` and picks up the current config — including after a hot-reload.
- What changed: `src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts` (conditional runtime metadata caching)
- What did NOT change: `resolveSessionModelRef` (unchanged); override model resolution (still cached); hot-reload handler; session persistence; `/new` inheritance

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #102269
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

The gateway logs `config hot reload applied (agents.list)` after changing `agents.<id>.model.primary`, but session model resolution keeps returning the pre-change value. The stale session runtime metadata (`modelProvider`/`model`) was treated as authoritative over current config defaults. Fixing this eliminates the need for a full gateway restart to pick up a model config change.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Session entries cache `modelProvider`/`model` from agent default during reset, and these become stale after a config hot-reload.
- Real environment tested: Linux (Node 24), `fix/session-model-hot-reload-102269` branch.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts --run
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/tools-effective.global-agent.integration.test.ts --run
  ```

- Evidence after fix:

  ```console
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts --run
   Test Files  4 passed (4)
        Tests  480 passed (480)

  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/tools-effective.global-agent.integration.test.ts --run
   Test Files  2 passed (2)
        Tests  4 passed (4)
  ```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. New sessions reset without user overrides → `modelProvider`/`model` not cached → next `resolveSessionModelRef` falls through to `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` → picks up current config (including hot-reloaded model)
  2. Sessions with user override → `modelProvider`/`model` still cached from override → override model preserved after hot-reload
  3. Sessions created before this fix (with stale cached metadata) → unaffected until next reset (`/new`, daily, compaction) → after reset, new model picked up
  4. Integration test (non-default `modelProvider`/`model` without overrides) → unchanged behavior (not a regression)
- What was not tested: Full E2E hot-reload lifecycle with file watcher (requires provider credentials); the fix is proven at the reset-origin level by unit and integration tests

## Root Cause (if applicable)

After a session reset (`performGatewaySessionReset` in `session-reset-service.ts:1127-1128`), the resolved model was always stored as `modelProvider`/`model` on the session entry. When the model came from agent defaults (no user overrides), this created a cached copy of the default that `resolveSessionModelRef` (`session-utils.ts:1647-1648`) returned directly on subsequent calls — ignoring future config changes. The hot-reload handler (`server-reload-handlers.ts`) correctly resets the model catalog but has no mechanism to invalidate per-session metadata. `/new` child sessions inherit stale values through `inheritSessionRuntimeSelection` (`session-create-service.ts:124-125`).

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

After changing `agents.<id>.model.primary` and triggering a config hot-reload, new turns and fresh threads (created via `/new`) now pick up the new model immediately instead of remaining on the stale pre-reload model.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Reset with/without user overrides; override model preserved after reset; hot-reload picks up new default after reset
- Edge cases checked: Non-default `modelProvider`/`model` without overrides (channel model routing) — unchanged and unaffected; subagent sessions with fallback origin tracking — unchanged; explicit `model:null` patch — clears runtime metadata correctly
- What you did NOT verify: Full E2E hot-reload lifecycle with file watcher (requires provider credentials); smoke-test of all channels

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — all existing tests pass without modification; query-time behavior (`resolveSessionModelRef`) is completely unchanged
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Not caching agent-default-derived runtime metadata at the reset source is strictly more correct than guessing staleness at query time. It eliminates the root cause (the cache should never have existed for default-derived values) without adding any query-time branching that could mis-classify legitimate non-default runtime metadata.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: 
  1. Query-time staleness check in `resolveSessionModelRef` — rejected because it cannot distinguish stale defaults from legitimate non-default runtime metadata, as confirmed by the CI failure in v1 of this PR
  2. Hot-reload handler invalidation — rejected because iterating session stores during reload is complex, has race conditions, and doesn't prevent the same staleness from re-accumulating

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: Sessions created before this fix that have stale cached metadata (`modelProvider`/`model` from old default, no overrides) won't be corrected until their next reset (`/new`, daily, compaction). This is acceptable because: (a) the stale cache already existed and this PR doesn't make it worse, (b) every session eventually resets through normal use, and (c) the hot-reload was already not working for these sessions, so this fix doesn't regress behavior.
- **Mitigation**: Clear and bounded — once a session resets it picks up the current config. Follow-up work could eagerly clear stale metadata on startup or hot-reload for stronger guarantees.
- **Compatibility**: No breaking changes. All existing tests pass. The `resolveSessionModelRef` query path is completely unchanged; only the reset-side caching policy changed.

---

Related to #102269
